routes.note: ThreadController override of mail.controllers.thread.ThreadController.mail_message_post - forwards canned_response_ids into request context so the onboarding_canned step can detect canned-response usage

security.note: mail_bot defines NO own security artifacts; the odoobot_state field is exposed only under base.group_no_one in the inherited res.users form and the partner is base.partner_root (OdooBot)

behavioral_notes.observation: mail_bot.py:14/54 - OdooBot is a scripted, rule-based reply engine (NO LLM/AI). _apply_logic short-circuits unless the message is a non-bot 'comment' (or a command); it lowercases/normalizes the body, then _get_answer branches ONLY when channel.channel_type=='chat' AND base.partner_root is a member. Replies are keyed jointly on res.users.odoobot_state and on message content: onboarding_emoji needs _body_contains_emoji, onboarding_command needs command=='help', onboarding_ping needs OdooBot's partner id in values['partner_ids'], onboarding_attachement needs values['attachment_ids'], onboarding_canned needs context['canned_response_ids']; each matched step advances odoobot_state and clears odoobot_failed, then posts the next scripted Markup message. Mismatches set odoobot_failed=True and re-prompt; 'idle' yields help/easter-egg replies. None of this branching logic is visible in metadata - it lives entirely in Python.

discuss_channel.py:13 - mail_bot inherits discuss.channel and overrides _message_post_after_hook to call self.env['mail.bot']._apply_logic(self, msg_vals) on EVERY message posted to ANY channel, BEFORE super(). The bot's own _apply_logic then self-filters (author != odoobot, type=='comment', chat channel with odoobot member), so the reply is a side-effect of a normal user message_post - the bot's answer is itself posted via channel.sudo().message_post(author_id=odoobot, silent=True). execute_command_help is also overridden so the '/help' slash command feeds _apply_logic with command='help' (drives the onboarding_command step).

res_users.py:28/33 - OdooBot is the existing base.partner_root partner (resolved via ir.model.data _xmlid_to_res_id('base.partner_root')); there is no dedicated bot user creation. _on_webclient_bootstrap fires _init_odoobot the first time an internal user (_is_internal) loads the webclient while odoobot_state is False/not_initialized: it _get_or_create_chat between odoobot and the user's partner, posts the 'Hello / Try to send me an emoji :)' greeting, and sets odoobot_state='onboarding_emoji', launching the onboarding tour. mailbot_data.xml sets base.user_root's odoobot_state='disabled' so the admin/root user is excluded from onboarding.

mail_bot.py:89-118 - the onboarding_attachement step CREATES a temporary mail.canned.response ('Thanks' -> 'Thanks for your feedback. Goodbye!') so the user can try '::'; the onboarding_canned step UNLINKS that temporary canned response (filtered by create_uid + source) once used, then sets odoobot_state='idle'. odoobot_state (Selection) and odoobot_failed (Boolean) are stored, readonly res.users fields; odoobot_state is added to SELF_READABLE_FIELDS so the web client can read its own onboarding progress. Re-running 'start the tour' from idle restarts at onboarding_emoji.

0 JS files, 0 OWL components, 0 registry registrations, 0 patches; only static asset is mail_bot/static/src/scss/odoobot_style.scss in web.assets_backend (styles the o_odoobot_command span used in scripted replies). All chat UI is inherited from the mail (Discuss) frontend; mail_bot ships no client components of its own.

0 outbound HTTP call sites; no SDK imports; uses_api_keys=False. The only external references are inert documentation/help URLs embedded in scripted replies (odoo.com/documentation, odoo.com/slides) and the manifest website (odoo.com/app/discuss) - rendered as links, never called server-side.

it_architecture.application: mail_bot (OdooBot - scripted onboarding chatbot layered on the Discuss/mail messaging subsystem)
logical_data_erm: mail.bot -> discuss.channel (operates on, no FK; AbstractModel)
discuss.channel -> mail.message (bot reply posted as author_id=base.partner_root)
res.users -> res.partner (partner_id used to open the OdooBot chat)
information_flows: side-effect: user message_post on a chat channel -> discuss.channel._message_post_after_hook -> mail.bot._apply_logic -> (if matched) odoobot reply message_post
side-effect: first webclient bootstrap (internal user) -> res.users._init_odoobot -> create OdooBot chat + greeting + odoobot_state='onboarding_emoji'
side-effect: onboarding_attachement step -> create temporary mail.canned.response; onboarding_canned step -> unlink it
control-flow: odoobot_state (res.users) is the conversation-state variable threading every scripted step

capabilities: User Onboarding / Product Discovery (scripted Discuss tour)
Conversational Assistance (rule-based OdooBot replies, help links)
Feature Walkthrough Orchestration (emoji -> command -> ping -> attachment -> canned response)
value_streams: Onboard-New-User: first webclient load -> auto-open OdooBot chat + greeting -> guide through emoji/command/ping/attachment/canned steps -> mark idle (onboarding complete)
Assist-On-Demand: user message/'/help' in OdooBot chat -> match state+content -> scripted reply or documentation/video links
organization: base.group_no_one (debug - only context that exposes odoobot_state in the user form)
policies: Onboarding runs only for internal users (_is_internal) with odoobot_state in {False, not_initialized}; share/portal users excluded
base.user_root is hard-set to odoobot_state='disabled' (admin excluded from onboarding)
Bot replies only in channel_type=='chat' channels where base.partner_root is a member, and never to its own messages
Each scripted step gates on both odoobot_state and message content; failure sets odoobot_failed and re-prompts
metrics: res.users.odoobot_state distribution (onboarding funnel: emoji -> command -> ping -> attachment -> canned -> idle)
res.users.odoobot_failed counts (users stuck / re-prompted at a step)

classification.rationale: mail_bot (OdooBot) is a cross-cutting SUPPORT subsystem (Stabell & Fjeldstad): it owns no business object of its own (mail.bot is an AbstractModel; it only adds two state fields to res.users and hooks discuss.channel), and produces no product or revenue document. Its entire purpose is internal onboarding and self-service assistance on top of the messaging layer - guiding new internal users through Discuss features via a scripted state machine. This is internal-communications / employee-enablement infrastructure consumed by users of every primary activity, never part of a primary value chain. APQC best fit is 9.4 'Manage internal communications' (user onboarding/assistance broadcast to internal staff); a defensible alternative is 13.0 'Develop and Manage Business Capabilities' (knowledge/enablement), but 9.4 is closer because the deliverable is a guided internal conversation, not a managed capability asset. activity_class=support follows directly: it is enabling infrastructure, not a customer-facing or production primary activity.

standard_capabilities: Auto-launched OdooBot onboarding chat on first webclient load for internal users
Scripted, content+state keyed walkthrough: emoji -> /command -> @ping -> attachment -> :: canned response -> idle
Rule-based help/easter-egg replies with links to Odoo documentation and video slides
Per-user onboarding progress tracked in res.users.odoobot_state (re-runnable via 'start the tour')
Temporary canned-response creation/cleanup to demonstrate the '::' feature
typical_fits: Out-of-the-box new-employee Discuss onboarding with zero configuration (auto_install with mail)
Disable onboarding for a user by setting odoobot_state='disabled' (as done for base.user_root)
common_gaps: No real NLU/AI - replies are hard-coded string/state matches; cannot answer free-form questions
Onboarding script content/branches are not configurable from the UI (Python-defined)
Single fixed persona (base.partner_root); no per-company or branded bot
Emoji detection relies on a static hard-coded Unicode range list that can drift from newer emoji sets
